newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's top police chief resigns.
newsitem.headline: Japan's top police chief resigns.

text.p: Japan's national police chief Takaji Kunimatsu resigned on Tuesday, two days before the second anniversary of the Tokyo subway gas attack which changed Japan's image of itself as a safe society.
The subway attack nearly cost Kunimatsu his own life and in the end was the event that he said indirectly led him to step down.
On March 30, 1995, just ten days after the poison gas attack, Kunimatsu was shot four times from about 20 yards (metres) away by a masked man as he left his apartment in central Tokyo.
In announcing his resignation at a news conference, Kunimatsu said he blamed himself for his shooting.
"I was careless to be shot. I painfully feel responsible," he said. "But I don't think I bear any legal or institutional responsibility," he added.

As Japan's top policeman, Kunimatsu was responsible for massive and repeated police raids on the doomsday cult Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth Sect) accused of the Tokyo subway attacks in which 12 peole were killed and thousands were hurt.
A former police officer who belonged to the cult had told investigators he shot Kunimatsu.

But although the former officer was fired from the Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department last year for leaking police information to the cult, he has not been arrested despite his confession because of lack of evidence.
The Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department came under harsh public criticism for an alleged cover-up surrounding the shooting of the national police chief.
For five months, Tokyo police investigators failed to report that one of their own officers had confessed to shooting Kunimatsu.
In November, Superintendent General Yukihiko Inoue, chief of the Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department, stepped down over his department's handling of the attempted assassination.
Kunimatsu said that with order restored to the police system after the cover-up, he felt it was now time for him to resign.
His replacement has not yet been announced.
